recipes.name: Super Simple Oven-Barbequed Chicken
ingredients_raw: 6 bone-in chicken breast halves, with skin

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Spray a 9x13-inch baking dish with cooking spray.

Arrange chicken, skin-side up, in the prepared baking dish, leaving a bit of room between each piece. Drizzle chicken with Worcestershire sauce and liquid smoke, then sprinkle with chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, thyme, oregano, salt, and pepper. Cover with aluminum foil.
Bake in the preheated oven until no longer pink at the bone and the juices run clear, 1 to 1 1/2 hours. An instant-read thermometer inserted near the bone should read 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Super Simple Oven-Barbequed Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Chicken roasted in the oven with liquid smoke, Worcestershire, herbs, and spices is much easier than — and gives almost the same results as — cooking it on the grill.

review.reviewBody: I've made this recipe twice now...so obviously I think it's great. I rubbed a little vegetable oil over the chicken before sprinkling with the spice rub and let it "marinate" in the refrigerator overnight. Then sprinkled with the worcestershire sauce before baking. For a nice variation try equal amounts of paprika, cumin, turmeric, garlic and brown sugar. I covered the baking dish with foil and baked about 50 mins covered and 10 minutes uncovered. Used chicken breasts the first time and thighs the next. Both were delicious - moist and flavorful.

I've made chicken breasts and thighs (waaaayyy better)using nearly this exact recipe for over 30 years. Three things,.... 1. I brine mine for 2-3 hours (salt,brown sugar, vegetable base, peppercorns) to guarantee juiciness with tons of added flavor. 2. Try roasting using a sheet pan with wire rack instead of the meat lying in a puddle of grease. 3. Will somebody tell these people that don't eat the skin that once 'roasted' chicken skin becomes crispy it's because all, or nearly all of the fat has rendered out, leaving leaving an extremely tasty fat free treat behind.

Guilty of using a recipe as a suggestion. 5 lb chicken, spatchcocked. Increased Worcestershire sauce and liquid smoke to 2 Tbs. Added 1 Tbs of vegetable oil to herbs and spices to make a thick paste. Oven at 425 for an hour. Yummy!
Love love love this recipie, the only thing I added was at the end a 1/4 cup of baby ray's honey BBQ sauce in the juices in the bottom of pan 30 min before chicken was ready and basted often YUM!!
This was delicious. Easy to make, moist, flavorful, and yummy????????. I added d barbecue sauce and basted the chicken. That made this a 5 star favorite????
I loved this! I used thighs and I also rubbed the BBQ sauce under the skin. It's so quick and easy and delicious!

I really was not sure if I would like this. It was wonderful. I used all the correct ingredients and amounts, just did it slightly different by putting them all in the bowl to make a "paste", added chicken and let it hang out for 2 hours then grilled it. Turned out great! On the gas grill it tasted like it was done in a smoker or charcoal grill. Will definitely do again, possibly on skewers next time!

my family really loved this one... i DID make more sauce like others have suggested and brushed the marinade on constantly throughout cook time and they came out perfect thanks!! will make many more times!
Flavorful and moist. I also added a tablespoon of brown sugar and used a meat thermomter, because I used boneless breasts. Quick and easy!

This was excellent. I will definitely make it again. The only changes I made was to sprinkle on a little paprika in addition to the other spices. I also baked it for just over an hour for 3 large chicken breasts and it came out perfectly. It was so moist, tender, and flavorful I didn't think any other BBQ sauce was necessary.

This gets 5 stars for easy to fix and the end result was pretty good too. Extremely moist chicken that smelled wonderful the entire time I was cooking it. Using a meat thermometer to test for doneness, 4 large breasts were easily cooked in about an hour. I then brushed them with BBQ sauce and let them bake a few minutes more. This recipe allows you to prepare these without standing over the grill. An added bonuse for me, was avoiding the blackened and burnt BBQ sauce that happens easily when I am trying to grill chicken and do other meal prep work.
Definitely needed more liquid. 2 tablespoons total, just wasn't enough. Very dry.
This was super easy, and tasty too! Skin got nice a crispy. Thanks!!

I left the skin of, which created a juicy meat, but since neither my husband or I actually eat the skin, all the seasonings failed to flavor the meat. I'll try it again but this time, pull the skin off and flavor directly onto the meat.
Totally loved it, so easy, and tastes like the real outdoor thing. Two comments -1) sprinkle a bit of oil on the chicken breasts before covering 2) VERY loosely with the foil.
best chicken ever!! boyfriend and i agreed this is one of the best recipes i've tried yet!
